title: CALL USING marshals every argument out of WORKING-STORAGE, whatever section it is declared in
description:
interpreter/cobol/lower_call.py:47 binds ws_reg from materialised.working_storage and line 60 does 'fl, _ = materialised.resolve(param.name)', DISCARDING the owning region that resolve returns. Copy-in and copy-back then both use ws_reg unconditionally.

So a CALL USING argument declared in LINKAGE or LOCAL-STORAGE is marshalled from the WORKING-STORAGE region at the field's offset-within-its-own-section. The callee receives whatever bytes happen to sit at that offset in WS.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (not by inspection). Probe: WS = [WS-ALPHA X(10), WS-BETA X(8)], LINKAGE = [LK-FOO X(8)]. resolve('LK-FOO') returns offset 0, length 8, owning region %1 (LINKAGE). The emitted LoadRegion reads region %0 (WORKING-STORAGE) at offset 0 length 8 — i.e. the first 8 bytes of WS-ALPHA. Repeating with LOCAL-STORAGE [LS-BAR X(4)]: owning region %2, CALL reads %0. Both sections affected; resolve's precedence is LOCAL-STORAGE > WORKING-STORAGE > LINKAGE, so any argument not in WS is wrong.

WORSE ON BY REFERENCE: the copy-back WriteRegion also targets ws_reg at the same offset, so the callee's output is written ON TOP of the unrelated WS field. It is not only a bad read — it silently corrupts WORKING-STORAGE on return.

Why it survived: the false invariant is asserted in the code rather than checked. lower_call.py:51 says '# Resolve field layouts for all USING params (all are in WS).' and the docstring repeats 'Copy each USING field from WS'. MaterialisedSectionedLayout.resolve was later given a region return value and this caller was never updated.

REACHABILITY: passing a LINKAGE item to a further CALL is the standard 'hand my caller's parameter down' pattern and is common in production COBOL.

SIBLING, SAME FAMILY: statement_dispatch.py:100 passes only the WS (layout, region) pair to lower_move_corresponding, with the comment 'uses first WS section' — so MOVE CORRESPONDING on a LINKAGE or LOCAL-STORAGE group has the same defect. Filed here because the fix is the same shape.

NOT a bug, checked: lower_search.py:48 discards the region but only reads fl.occurs_count. lower_arithmetic.py:641 _find_group_and_reg iterates the sections and returns the matching (layout, reg) pair — that is the correct existing pattern to model the fix on.
acceptance_criteria: A CALL USING an argument declared in LINKAGE marshals from the LINKAGE region, and a BY REFERENCE copy-back writes to the LINKAGE region — asserted on emitted IR and on an executed program whose callee mutates the argument. Same for LOCAL-STORAGE. MOVE CORRESPONDING on a non-WS group resolves against its own section.
notes:
CORRECTION to the sibling claim in the description. I wrote that MOVE CORRESPONDING 'has the same defect'. It does not — verified by probe: MOVE CORRESPONDING from a LINKAGE group raises loudly,

  KeyError: "Group not found in layout: 'LK-REC'"

because lower_move_corresponding (lower_arithmetic.py:610) receives one DataLayout and one Register for BOTH operands, and lookup_group on the WS layout misses. So it is a LOUD unsupported-case, not silent corruption — a materially lower severity than the CALL bug, and it should not be conflated with it.

The real MOVE CORRESPONDING limitation is structural: a single (layout, region) pair cannot express operands in two different sections, and MOVE CORRESPONDING LK-REC TO WS-REC is the common shape. Fixing it means giving it a per-operand region, the way _find_group_and_reg (lower_arithmetic.py:634) already resolves them.

The CALL USING bug in the description stands as verified.
close_reason:
Fixed in red-dragon e1e8875d, vendored here as a1af3a1f.

lower_call now takes the owning region from materialised.resolve per parameter, for both copy-in and BY REFERENCE copy-back. Per option 2 of the brainstorm it also stops binding a whole-section register while marshalling at all — the WS region is bound only at the one line that legitimately needs it (restoring the caller's __ws_region after the call) — so there is no section-wide register in scope to reach for by mistake.

Proven at runtime, not just on IR: a new integration test chains CHAINA -> CHAINB -> CHAINC, where CHAINB hands its LINKAGE item down. Before the fix CHAINC received 9999 (CHAINB's WS-DECOY) instead of 5. A unit test locks both LINKAGE and LOCAL-STORAGE at the IR level and was mutation-checked — reverting the fix turns it red.

red-dragon suite: 15065 passed, 66 skipped, 17 xfailed, no regressions. cicada 449 passed, forge 62 passed against the bump.

NOT fixed here, deliberately: the MOVE CORRESPONDING limitation recorded in the notes. It raises loudly rather than corrupting, so it is a different severity and belongs in its own change — lower_move_corresponding takes a single (layout, region) pair and cannot express operands in two sections.

title: CICS prepass injects copybooks into the main source only, so CALLed subprograms using HANDLE CONDITION cannot compile
description:
build_cics_spec's source_prepass is folded over the MAIN source only (interpreter.project.coprocessor_compile.compile_program), so DFHEIBLK and DFHHANDLE are never injected into a disk-resolved CALL callee or an extra_subprogram_sources module. A subprogram containing EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION therefore fails to compile unless it carries its own COPY DFHHANDLE by hand.

Found while adding the multi-module isolation test in Task 5 of the condition-handling plan (commit 4c58a1e5): cicada/tests/integration/cics/test_condition_handling.py's HNDLINKB fixture works around this with an explicit COPY DFHHANDLE, which real corpus subprograms will not have.

Same gap applies to EIBRESP references (DFHEIBLK) in any CALLed subprogram, so it is broader than condition handling.
acceptance_criteria: A CALLed subprogram containing EXEC CICS HANDLE CONDITION, with no hand-written COPY DFHHANDLE, compiles and numbers its own handlers. The HNDLINKB fixture's explicit COPY DFHHANDLE can be removed and its test still passes.
notes: Confirmed live in Task 6 (commit 396bf478): a callee needs BOTH copybooks, not just DFHHANDLE. COPY DFHHANDLE. supplies DFH-HANDLER/DFH-RAISABLE; COPY DFHEIBLK. supplies EIBRESP. The Task 5 HNDLINKB fixture had only the former and tripped the new guard, which is the guard working as intended. CicsLoweringStrategy._emit_dispatcher_if_needed now raises NotImplementedError naming this bead when a module registers handlers but lacks either field.

title: squall-db2: the Db2 instance dies repeatedly while the container stays up
description:
The local Db2 test container dies several times a day, failing every Db2-backed suite with SQL30081N and blocking any commit (the tests-forge and tests-squall pre-commit hooks both need it). Hit 4 times in one session on 2026-09-02, twice mid-commit.

DIAGNOSIS (measured, not inferred):

  docker inspect squall-db2 --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'  ->  true
  docker stats squall-db2                                    ->  mem 223MiB / 1.91GiB
  .HostConfig.Memory                                         ->  0  (no limit set)
  .RestartCount                                              ->  0  (container never restarted)
  Health.FailingStreak                                       ->  420

The kernel OOM killer is killing Db2's engine processes inside the container while
the CONTAINER ITSELF stays up. That is why the symptom looks like a dropped TCP
listener but a local connect reports:

  SQL1032N  No start database manager command was issued.  SQLSTATE=57019

i.e. the database manager is not running AT ALL — it is not a listener problem.

Two consequences worth separating:

1. squall/Makefile's db2-restart comment is wrong about the mechanism. It says 'the
   listener can occasionally drop ... while a local connect still works'. A local
   connect does NOT still work — the instance is dead. The recipe (db2stop force;
   db2start) happens to fix it because db2start revives the instance; the db2stop
   reports SQL1032N because there is nothing to stop.
2. The healthcheck is CORRECT to report unhealthy and had a failing streak of 420,
   but make db2-up treats unhealthy as fatal (prints logs, exit 1) — so once this
   happens, db2-up refuses to bring the environment up even though db2-restart
   fixes it in seconds. A contributor following the README gets a dead end.

Likely fix: Db2 11.5.9 community wants ~4GB; the Docker VM here has 1.91GiB total,
and the image runs under amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon which inflates its
footprint. Options: raise the Docker Desktop VM memory allocation; set an explicit
mem_limit/reservation in squall/docker-compose.yml so the failure is a clear
container OOM rather than a silent engine death; and/or cap Db2's own appetite via
INSTANCE_MEMORY / DB2_LIMIT_MEMORY so it sizes itself to what is actually there.
design: Investigate in this order: (1) confirm the OOM by correlating .State.OOMKilled with the db2diag entries at the death timestamps; (2) measure what the instance actually needs under emulation (db2 get dbm cfg | grep INSTANCE_MEMORY — the default AUTOMATIC will size to host RAM the VM does not have); (3) prefer capping Db2 (INSTANCE_MEMORY to a fixed value) over raising the VM, since CI runs native amd64 and should not need the same tuning. Add a mem_limit to docker-compose.yml either way so a future OOM kills the container visibly instead of leaving a zombie that reports healthy-ish.
acceptance_criteria: The container survives a full working day of repeated test runs without the instance dying; if it does die, docker reports it (container exits/restarts) rather than staying up with a dead database manager. make db2-up recovers a container in this state instead of exiting 1. squall/Makefile's db2-restart comment describes the real mechanism.
notes:
FOLLOW-UP EVIDENCE 2026-09-04: the INSTANCE_MEMORY cap is NOT sufficient. Measured on a container that had been up 23h and still reported (healthy):

  db2 get dbm cfg | grep INSTANCE_MEMORY  ->  262144   (the documented 1 GiB cap, still in place)
  dmesg                                   ->  Out of memory: Killed process (db2sysc)
                                             total-vm:9077392kB anon-rss:4828532kB shmem-rss:315168kB
                                             oom-kill: constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE ... global_oom

So db2sysc reached ~4.8 GiB resident / ~9 GiB mapped WITH the cap applied. INSTANCE_MEMORY bounds database manager shared memory; it does not bound agent private memory or the process's total footprint, which is what the kernel actually kills on. The README currently claims the cap makes the container settle around 1 GiB -- that claim is disproven and has been corrected.

Still-true parts of the original diagnosis: container stays up and reports healthy while the engine is dead; global_oom means the VM ran out, so a per-container mem_limit will not help; 'make db2-restart' revives it in ~15s.

Open question for whoever picks this up: cap agent private memory too, or give the VM enough headroom for db2sysc's real ceiling rather than its configured one.

title: No EXEC CICS condition is ever raised — every error path runs on stale data
description:
The half of condition handling that is NOT red-dragon-pz9g.12. That bead covers the handler table and dispatch; this one covers the fact that there is nothing to dispatch ON.

emit_resp_writeback (cics/strategy.py:277-293) writes the response code into EIBRESP and the RESP(name) field and stops. No branch, no abend, no signal. NOHANDLE appears nowhere in strategy.py — self-consistently, since every verb already behaves as though NOHANDLE were coded.

Real CICS, on a non-NORMAL condition with neither RESP nor NOHANDLE, transfers control to the registered HANDLE CONDITION label, or abends the task if none is registered. Here execution continues to the next statement with whatever was in the target area before the failed operation. A program whose entire error strategy is HANDLE CONDITION MAPFAIL(...) proceeds THROUGH the failure, silently, on stale data.

Blast radius (production online corpus): 2,679 HANDLE CONDITION occurrences across 1,599 of 2,137 programs — 75%. The corpus's error paths are written this way throughout.
design: Raising and dispatch must land together (see the sequencing note in the analysis). Implementing raising FIRST converts a large number of currently-silent wrong answers into abends: an improvement in truthfulness that will read as a regression in any pass/fail count. Either land both, or expect the noise and say so up front.
acceptance_criteria: A failing command with no RESP/NOHANDLE and no registered handler abends the task; with a handler it transfers to the label; with RESP or NOHANDLE it continues as today. Tests assert control flow, not just EIBRESP.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect F. Note the plan referenced in the strategy.py comment (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-07-cics-handle-condition-machinery.md) DOES NOT EXIST in this repo — it never survived the monorepo migration. It must be rewritten from scratch; do not go looking for it.
close_reason:
Implemented across 1917ed0c..97ea2c61. HANDLE CONDITION and IGNORE CONDITION write an injected DFH-HANDLER table numbered at parse time; a raise tail after each command's EIBRESP writeback tests DFH-RAISABLE and branches to a per-program dispatcher that runs the registered paragraph or abends AEIZ. RESP and NOHANDLE suppress the raise. Recorded in docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md.

Deliberately left, each with its own bead: HANDLE AID still a no-op; PUSH/POP HANDLE; the eleven conditions outside the raisable nine; the per-condition AEIx abend mapping; NOTOPEN registered but unreachable; EXEC CICS LINK isolation untested; and forge-43l (the copybook prepass reaches the main source only).

title: EXEC CICS temporary storage: READQ/WRITEQ/DELETEQ TS unimplemented
description:
WRITEQ TD is implemented; the TS queue family is not. Occurrences in the production online corpus: DELETEQ TS 144, READQ TS 98, WRITEQ TS 88 (330 total).

All three currently emit no IR (see the unimplemented-verb policy bead), so a WRITEQ TS is a silent nop and a READQ TS leaves its INTO area holding whatever was there before — the classic stale-data wrong answer.

The three verbs share one store and must be designed together: a per-region queue map keyed by QUEUE name, ITEM-numbered records, with MAIN/AUXILIARY treated identically and REWRITE honoured. Queue lifetime is the open question — TS queues outlive a task and are typically how a pseudo-conversational flow carries state across turns, so the store belongs on the region, not the task.
acceptance_criteria: Write-then-read round-trips across two pseudo-conversational turns; ITEM numbering, REWRITE, NUMITEMS and QIDERR on a missing queue all covered.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table.

title: EXEC CICS BIF DEEDIT is unimplemented
description:
992 occurrences in the production online corpus — the second-highest unimplemented verb after START. Numeric de-editing of screen input: strips every non-digit from a field in place, right-justifies zero-filled. Programs use it on every numeric field a user types, so an unimplemented DEEDIT means screen input is consumed raw.

Falls through to the terminal 'unimplemented verb' warning (see the policy bead) and emits no IR, so the FIELD operand is left exactly as typed and nothing indicates it.
acceptance_criteria: BIF DEEDIT lowers to IR that de-edits the FIELD operand in place; test covers embedded spaces, currency/punctuation, a sign, and an all-non-digit field.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E verb table. The CICS grammar already parses it; the work is strategy.py lowering plus the de-edit builtin.

title: Unimplemented EXEC CICS verbs vanish silently — make them loud
description:
cics/strategy.py:1064 logs 'unimplemented verb %r — no IR emitted' and drops the statement. The program then runs on as if it had executed, so a run can skip its entire downstream flow, terminate on a normal RETURN, and look clean. First execution of a production program did exactly that: four skipped verbs, zero failures reported.

A logger.warning on a shared logger is not something a harness can assert on. This is the cross-cutting defect behind the whole family in docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md: a component that cannot do something should say so in its RETURN VALUE, not only in a log line.

Options in order of preference:
1. An unsupported_verbs strictness setting — raise at lowering time by default, warn only on opt-in.
2. Emit IR that abends at runtime naming the verb, so the failure lands where the program actually depended on it.
3. At minimum, surface the accumulated set of skipped verbs on the compile result.
design: Prefer (1)+(3) together: strictness setting for the default path, and the skipped-verb set on the compile result regardless of strictness so callers can assert. (2) is the fallback if lowering-time raise proves too blunt for bring-up.
acceptance_criteria: Compiling a program containing an unimplemented verb either raises or returns a result carrying the skipped verbs; a test asserts on the return value rather than on captured logs.
notes: Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E, 'Fix shape for the policy itself'. Blocks nothing, but every verb bead below is a silent wrong answer until this lands.

title: Reconcile cobol_expression: adopt cobble's dispatch table + 3 node kinds into red-dragon
description:
cobble/cobble/interpreter/cobol/cobol_expression.py is 294 lines ahead of red-dragon's: a _BUILDERS dispatch table keyed by bridge 'kind', FigurativeNode/LengthOfNode/DfhRespNode (without which one unknown operand kind raises out of CobolASG.from_dict and costs a whole program's ASG -- COMPUTE WS-PCT = ZEROES), and a ToFieldEnd sentinel replacing RefModNode.ref_mod_length=None.

Blocks repointing cobble's ref_mod, cics_visitor, statements and cics_parser: those pull red-dragon's older expression vocabulary in with them and split LiteralNode into two classes (caught by cobble's own suite during the wave-1 integration).

NOT mechanical. red-dragon's condition_lowering.py must be taught what the three new node kinds mean, or its existing 'unknown node -> const 0 / ref name' fallbacks turn a loud ValueError into silently wrong IR: a figurative lowers to 0 (right for ZEROS, wrong for SPACES/HIGH-VALUES/LOW-VALUES) and LENGTH OF becomes a ref to a field named ''. ToFieldEnd likewise changes a contract the lowering reads.

Land in ~/code/red-dragon, then bump forge's submodule.

title: A lone unresolved JCL symbol in DSN raises, losing the whole job's graph
description:
z/OS reads DSN=&NAME as DSN=&&NAME when NAME is no defined symbol, and production JCL relies on it: a job writes DSN=&WORK in the step that creates a work file and DSN=&&WORK in the step that reads it back.

jackal/dsn.py raises ValueError when a DirectDSN's Value has an unresolved Symbol part (documented at dsn.py:60). The graph builder takes the surviving symbol as a name to resolve, the lookup raises, and the raise escapes the pass — so the job loses every step, program and dataset it had, over one temporary file. Six members failed this way on cobble's corpus.

Fix (cobble d4771e4 + 805f3f4): temp_if_unresolved re-reads a DirectDSN whose whole value is a single symbol of at most 8 characters (a DSN qualifier's limit) as a TempRef, which the DD loop already skips — a temp lives and dies inside one job, so it carries no cross-job identity. A longer symbol, or one glued to literal text (&HLQ..DATA), is an unbound parameter rather than a temp file and must stay the failure it is; guessing otherwise would invent a fact. 805f3f4 extends the same reading to a PROC's lone unbound DSN symbol.

Placement constraint: the classification must happen in the graph pass, NOT at parse time. PROC symbol substitution runs after the parse and matches DirectDSN, so reclassifying DSN=&INFILE early would break the substitution that gives it a value.

Note cobble rewrote jcl_graph.py alongside this (it had no unit tests and 28 fp-lint violations), pinning existing behaviour with tests first — including the known limit that two same-named outer steps calling PROCs cannot be told apart — then rebuilding the job walk as composition over per-DD and per-step graphs.

Same defect shape as the expression-kinds and dialect-parser bugs: one unknown input is fatal to the whole unit of work.
notes:
Placement is load-bearing: cobble put temp_if_unresolved in the GRAPH pass, not in dsn.py. Its stated reason is that PROC symbol substitution matches DirectDSN and runs after the parse, so reclassifying DSN=&INFILE early would break the substitution that gives it a value.

That placement also happens to leave jackal's EXECUTION path (runner, catalog) untouched, which cobble neither needed nor verified — it only builds graphs. Adopting this must preserve the placement; moving it down into dsn.py as a 'simplification' would change what the runner and catalog resolve, and cobble's tests would not catch it.

title: expr_from_dict rejects three expression kinds the bridge emits, losing the whole program's ASG
description:
interpreter/cobol/cobol_expression.py's expr_from_dict handles five 'kind' values — lit, ref, binop, neg, function — and raises ValueError on anything else. The ProLeap bridge in the SAME repository emits three more: figurative, dfhresp and length_of (see StatementSerializer.java). The bridge and its own deserializer disagree.

The raise escapes CobolASG.from_dict, so the program loses every fact it had over one operand. The trigger is ordinary COBOL: COMPUTE WS-PCT = ZEROES yields {'kind': 'figurative'} and fails with

    ValueError: Unknown expression node kind: 'figurative'

Found in cobble, where it surfaced as FILE-CONTROL failures on members whose only unusual construct was a figurative constant.

Fix (cobble 2715ca5): add FigurativeNode (bridge's canonical spelling, so ZERO/ZEROS/ZEROES all arrive as ZEROS), LengthOfNode (a compile-time byte count, deliberately NOT a FieldRefNode so consumers counting data reads do not miscount it), and DfhRespNode (the condition name, since the number the CICS translator substitutes is release-dependent). All three must round-trip through expr_to_dict. Cobble also converts the two if-chains into dispatch tables keyed by kind and node type, which makes the bridge/deserializer correspondence checkable — the next divergence becomes a missing row rather than a lost member.

Same defect shape as forge-<dialect-parsers> and the unresolved-JCL-symbol bug: one unknown input is fatal to the whole unit of work. Red-dragon change: fix in ~/code/red-dragon, then bump the submodule pointer.

title: Map XML GENERATE through red-dragon's ProLeap bridge and statement dispatch
description:
Depends on the ProLeap pin bump: once the fork parses XML GENERATE, the bridge sees a statement type it has no serializer for, falls through to serializeUnknown (type name and nothing else), and the Python dispatch has no entry, so parse_statement raises and takes the whole program's ASG down.

Import from cobble:
- StatementSerializer.serializeXmlGenerate: emits xml_document (receiver), from_record, count_in, and the ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION statement lists, matching how START and DELETE serialize their conditional phrases.
- XmlGenerateSerializerTest + src/test/resources/fixtures/xml_generate.cbl.
- interpreter/cobol/cobol_statements.py: XmlGenerateStatement plus its dispatch entry, and the Python-side tests.

The statement contributes nothing to the flow graph (it converts a record to an XML document: transfers no control, names no file/queue/map). It is modelled because an unmodelled type is fatal to the program containing it.

title: Import cobble's JCL bridge grammar, two-stage parse and JUnit suite into jackal
description:
cobble/jcl-bridge is strictly ahead of jackal/jcl-bridge. Import:

- JclSerializer: two-stage parse (SLL + BailErrorStrategy, then full LL on bail). The top-level 'jcl : (execJCL+ SS?) | (procJCL SS?)' alternative is only decidable deep in the member, so full-context LL cost grows ~O(n^1.8): 2.0s for a 10 KB member, 25.7s for 46 KB, minutes for the largest. Also splits serialize() out of main() so the grammar-to-JSON path is testable without stdin/stdout/exit.
- JCLParser.g4: delimiterStatement permitted inside jclStep's DD list and in the statement loop (a bare /* between two DDs of one step ended the job and surfaced as 'mismatched input DD expecting JOB' at the next DD); parenList accepts an omitted last positional (SPACE=(CYL,(2,2,),RLSE)); ddParmBLKSIZE value optional.
- JCLLexer.g4: PROC_WS_SEQUENCE_FIELD + PROC_SEQUENCE_FIELD_MODE so a PROC with no parameter field does not lex its column-73 sequence number as a parameter.
- jcl-bridge/src/test: 6 JUnit test classes (DcbContinuation, DelimiterStatement, JclSerializer, OmittedPositional, NullDcbSubparameter, ProcSequenceNumber) - jackal's bridge currently has no tests.
- pom.xml: junit 4.13.2 test-scope dependency.

title: CICS SEND MAP / RECEIVE MAP: MAPSET, CURSOR, ERASE and FREEKB are dropped
description:
The BMS branch of CicsLoweringStrategy.lower() reads only MAP/MAPNAME and the FROM/INTO symbolic group. MAPSET, CURSOR, ERASE and FREEKB are parsed into stmt.options and then never looked at.

Usage-surface inventory over a real CICS corpus: SEND MAP 3 occ / 3 files, each carrying MAPSET, CURSOR, ERASE and FREEKB; RECEIVE MAP 3 occ / 3 files each carrying MAPSET.

Severity differs per option:
- MAPSET is a correctness risk. The map name is resolved on its own today, so two mapsets defining the same map name are indistinguishable. Harmless in a single-mapset corpus, wrong in general.
- ERASE (clear the screen before writing) and CURSOR (initial cursor position) are observable screen state. ScreenChannel would need to carry them.
- FREEKB (unlock the keyboard) has no analogue in the emulated terminal and can reasonably stay a documented nop rather than a silent one.
acceptance_criteria:
- MAPSET participates in map resolution rather than being ignored
- ERASE and CURSOR are conveyed to ScreenChannel, or explicitly documented as unmodelled
- FREEKB is an explicit, documented nop rather than a silent drop
- Test asserting a SEND MAP with ERASE/CURSOR reaches the screen channel with those attributes

title: CICS ASSIGN: only APPLID and SYSID are supported — USERID silently no-ops
description:
The ASSIGN branch of CicsLoweringStrategy.lower() iterates a hardcoded ('APPLID', 'SYSID') tuple, so any other sub-option is skipped: no builtin call, no write-back, no warning. make_assign_builtin(applid, sysid) likewise only knows those two values.

Usage-surface inventory over a real CICS corpus: ASSIGN 4 occ / 3 files, all of them USERID — i.e. every ASSIGN in the corpus is currently a nop, leaving the target field at whatever it already held.

USERID needs a source of truth. CicsRegion has no signed-on user concept today, so this issue includes deciding where the value comes from (constructor parameter on CicsLoweringStrategy alongside applid/sysid is the cheapest option, matching the existing shape).

A miss on an unrecognised sub-option should warn rather than silently skipping — that is what let this go unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria:
- ASSIGN USERID(f) writes a userid into f
- The userid source is explicit and configurable, not hardcoded at the call site
- An ASSIGN sub-option with no implementation logs a warning instead of being silently skipped
- Test covering ASSIGN USERID write-back
close_reason: Closed

title: CICS STARTBR: EQUAL and GENERIC are ignored — every browse starts GTEQ
description:
VsamEngine.startbr (cicada/cics/vsam/engine.py:210) hardcodes drv.start(key[:klen], '>='), and CicsLoweringStrategy's STARTBR branch never reads the EQUAL/GENERIC/GTEQ options at all — it passes only (file, key, keylength).

Usage-surface inventory over a real CICS corpus: GTEQ 37 occ / 5 files, EQUAL 3 occ / 3 files, GENERIC 3 occ / 2 files.

GTEQ is therefore accidentally correct. EQUAL is not: it must position only on an exact key match and return NOTFND otherwise, where the current code silently positions at the next higher key and reports RESP_NORMAL — a browse that should have found nothing instead walks the file from the wrong place. GENERIC (partial-key browse, keylength shorter than the full key) is also unhonoured as an explicit intent, though the existing keylength truncation makes it mostly behave.

The comment at engine.py:220 documents the past-end GTEQ seek-last idiom; that behaviour must be preserved for GTEQ while EQUAL takes the strict path.
acceptance_criteria:
- STARTBR lowering threads the positioning mode (EQUAL / GTEQ / GENERIC) through to the engine
- EQUAL positions only on exact match and yields NOTFND otherwise
- GTEQ keeps today's behaviour, including past-end positioning for the seek-last idiom
- GENERIC positions on the truncated key explicitly rather than incidentally
- Unit tests for all three modes against a seeded KSDS
close_reason: Closed

title: CICS interval control: START TRANSID and RETRIEVE are entirely unimplemented
description:
Usage-surface inventory (tools/mainframe_inventory.py) over a real CICS corpus reports 59 interval-control statements (CICS.AREA.INTERVAL_CONTROL, 7 files), of which the asynchronous-start pair is unimplemented:

  START TRANSID   13 occ / 4 files  (TERMID 12, FROM 9, LENGTH 8)
  RETRIEVE         3 occ / 3 files  (INTO 3, LENGTH 3)

Both verbs parse fine — CICSzParser.g4 covers them and cics_visitor.py maps
Start*/Retrieve* to 'START'/'RETRIEVE' — but CicsLoweringStrategy.lower() has no
branch for either. They fall through to the terminal
logger.warning('unimplemented verb %r — no IR emitted') and produce no IR at all,
so at runtime the statement is a silent nop: no task is scheduled, and a RETRIEVE
leaves its INTO field untouched with no indication anything went wrong.

This is a whole functional area rather than an option gap: START/RETRIEVE is how a
transaction hands data to a later-started task, so the two verbs need to be
designed together with a shared start-request store keyed by transid (+ termid),
and a dispatcher decision about when a started task actually runs.

Design questions to settle:
- Where do start requests live? Most likely alongside CicsRegion in cics/dispatcher.py.
- Does the emulation honour INTERVAL/AFTER/AT timing, or treat every START as
  immediate? Immediate-only is probably the right first slice; say so explicitly
  rather than silently ignoring the timing options.
- Does a started task get dispatched by the existing routing loop (_advance_routing)
  or does it need its own queue drain?
design:
Minimum viable shape:
1. Add DispatchKind.START (cics/types.py:18-22 currently has RETURN, RETURN_TRANSID, XCTL, ABEND only) plus transid, termid and start-data fields on DispatchResult.
2. Route it in _advance_routing (cics/dispatcher.py:95-107) the way RETURN_TRANSID is routed, carrying start data instead of a COMMAREA.
3. A per-terminal start-data store the runtime holds between tasks.
4. RETRIEVE reads that store into the INTO operand, with the usual EIBRESP writeback via emit_resp_writeback (strategy.py:277).

Two caveats to BUILD FOR rather than discover later:
- START in real CICS is ASYNCHRONOUS: it queues a task and the issuing task continues to its RETURN. Modelling it as a terminal dispatch is sound only while every START precedes a RETURN — true of every program surveyed, but NOT guaranteed. Assert it and abend loudly if a START is followed by more work.
- A program may issue several STARTs on different branches, so the store must be keyed by TERMID, not global.

Bring-up note: RETRIEVE is separately avoidable — every program surveyed guards it behind IF EIBCALEN = 0, so entering with a non-empty COMMAREA skips it. Useful for getting a flow running; not a substitute for the verb.
acceptance_criteria:
- EXEC CICS START TRANSID(...) TERMID(...) FROM(...) LENGTH(...) lowers to IR and records a start request
- EXEC CICS RETRIEVE INTO(...) LENGTH(...) recovers the FROM data of the START that began the task
- A started task is dispatched by the region and observes the retrieved data
- Unsupported timing options (INTERVAL/AFTER/AT) warn explicitly instead of being dropped
- Integration test covering a START -> dispatch -> RETRIEVE round trip
notes:
Re-measured 2026-09-02 on the full production online corpus (2,137 programs), far larger than the 7-file sample this bead was filed from: START 3,021 occurrences, RETRIEVE 920. START alone outranks every IMPLEMENTED verb except READ, RETURN and LINK. This is the top unimplemented verb by volume and the flow-control blocker for composition.

Analysis: docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md defect E, 'START / RETRIEVE design notes'. The parser is NOT the problem — cics_visitor.py's _CONTEXT_TO_VERB already maps Start->START (:280) and Retrieve->RETRIEVE (:244), and _extract_options delivers TRANSID/TERMID/FROM/LENGTH/INTERVAL/REQID and INTO/LENGTH fully parsed in opts. The work is entirely strategy.py lowering plus runtime plumbing — a smaller job than it looks.
close_reason:
Implemented earlier in this session (step 6 of the analysis document's suggested order), commits e33ec7ee..0f808ccb, recorded in docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md. START queues a request and does not end the task; RETRIEVE consumes it, ENDDATA when nothing started the task. Both drivers (CicsRegion and the blocking loop) drain the queue and carry a runaway guard; TRANSIDERR/TERMIDERR rejections are recorded on the queue. Missed at the time — closing now.

Left open deliberately, with their own beads: forge-6ze (an unbounded RETURN TRANSID self-loop when a driver never supplies input) and forge-95b (the two drivers disagree about which terminal a next-transid task gets).

title: CICS ASKTIME/FORMATTIME: ABSTIME operand ignored, missing date formats and DATESEP
description:
Usage-surface inventory (tools/mainframe_inventory.py) over a real CICS corpus shows 41 ASKTIME/FORMATTIME statements across 6 files whose ABSTIME plumbing is silently discarded, plus 18 uses of date formats cicada does not implement.

Three distinct defects in cicada/cics:

1. ASKTIME ABSTIME(field) never writes back (19 occ / 6 files).
   make_asktime_builtin() in cics/builtins/system.py computes a correct 1900-epoch
   abstime, but CicsLoweringStrategy.lower() dispatches ASKTIME through the generic
   _SYS_VERBS path, which only emits a write-back for verbs in _RESP_PRODUCING_VERBS
   (currently just INQUIRE). The returned value is dropped; the named field is
   never updated.

2. FORMATTIME ABSTIME(src) is ignored (22 occ / 6 files).
   The FORMATTIME branch of lower() iterates only the OUTPUT sub-options
   (YYYYMMDD/DATE/TIME) and calls __cics_formattime with just the sub-option key.
   make_formattime_builtin() formats datetime.now(timezone.utc) — it never sees the
   ABSTIME source. Programs that ASKTIME once and FORMATTIME the same abstime
   several times can observe skew, and any program formatting a stored/computed
   abstime gets the wall clock instead.

   These two mask each other: because (1) stores nothing, the field FORMATTIME
   would have read is empty anyway, so the current behaviour looks plausible.

3. Unimplemented output formats fall back silently (18 occ / 5 files).
   The 'formats' dict holds only YYYYMMDD/DATE/TIME. DDMMYYYY (6), DDMMYY (3) and
   YEAR (2) miss and hit the '%Y%m%d' default — a wrong string with no warning.
   DATESEP (7 occ / 4 files) is not handled at all, so no separator is inserted.
acceptance_criteria:
- ASKTIME ABSTIME(f) stores the abstime into f (via emit_copy_back_str, same path as ASSIGN)
- FORMATTIME ABSTIME(src) reads src and formats THAT value, not datetime.now()
- DDMMYYYY, DDMMYY and YEAR produce their correct formats
- DATESEP(c) inserts the separator (default '/' when the option has no argument)
- An unrecognised FORMATTIME sub-option warns rather than silently returning %Y%m%d
- Integration test: ASKTIME then two FORMATTIMEs of the same abstime yield identical, non-current values
notes:
Defect 3 (unimplemented output formats) is DONE: _DATE_PARTS in cics/builtins/system.py now covers DDMMYYYY, DDMMYY and YEAR, DATESEP is threaded from the lowering as a second builtin argument (bare DATESEP defaults to '/'), and an unrecognised sub-option warns instead of silently formatting as YYYYMMDD. DATESEP deliberately does not reach TIME — that is TIMESEP's job, and a test pins it.

REMAINING SCOPE: defects 1 and 2 only — ASKTIME ABSTIME(f) still discards the computed abstime (the generic _SYS_VERBS path writes back only for _RESP_PRODUCING_VERBS), and FORMATTIME still formats datetime.now() rather than the ABSTIME source.

title: Dataset/storage service: unified catalog + access API for all dataset consumers
description:
Datasets are the fundamental unit of mainframe storage interaction, and nearly every jackal component touches them — so dataset interaction should be ONE well-defined service that all consumers use, rather than each utility reaching into catalog internals + importing red-dragon drivers ad hoc. Build this FIRST; every os-runtime dataset feature (GDG, PDS, ESDS/RRDS, AIX, SORT, IEBGENER, IEBCOPY, DCB, concatenation) is a client of it.

CURRENT LEAK (the motivation): DatasetCatalog is the shared *catalog* API (resolve/allocate/dispose/delete_dsn), but (a) the *access* face is not an API — idcams/executor.py imports red-dragon IndexedDriver/SequentialDriver directly and opens them itself, while cobol_step takes catalog.allocate(dd).path and hands a raw Path to red-dragon's RealFileIOProvider (which uses the SAME drivers internally). Two consumers, two ways to reach a dataset's bytes. (b) allocate_ksds bakes one org into the catalog -> would sprawl to allocate_esds/rrds/pds/gdg.

TARGET (two clean faces, mirroring z/OS catalog + DADSM + access methods):
- CATALOG/BINDING face: resolve DSN->Dataset; allocate BY ORG (generalize allocate_ksds -> allocate(spec)); DISP lifecycle; GDG generation resolution; PDS member resolution. The parenthesized qualifier (gen/member) arrives structurally from the JCL grammar (no regex).
- ACCESS face: open-for-read / open-for-write by org -> a record reader/writer, wrapping red-dragon's drivers as the single access API. IDCAMS REPRO, SORT, IEBGENER all read/write through this instead of importing drivers.

CONSUMER-DRIVEN PRINCIPLE (binding instruction): the interfaces must be validated as consumable by EVERY consumer before they are fixed — IDCAMS (binding + access), COBOL steps (binding-ONLY; access is internal to the red-dragon VM via RealFileIOProvider), the runner DD allocate/dispose lifecycle, IEFBR14, and the forward consumers SORT/IEBGENER/IEBCOPY/GDG/PDS/ESDS/RRDS/AIX/DCB/concat. Build a consumer's slice against the API and adjust the API to fit, rather than designing it in isolation.

Constraints: FP/frozen, no None defaults, no defensive guards (fail loud), no regex. Brainstorm -> spec -> plan -> subagent-driven execution. This epic is a sibling to jackal-1o2 (JCL coverage), not a child — its own line of work.
notes:
SUBSTRATE AUDIT (2026-06-25) — design inputs from auditing red-dragon's file drivers + the CobolIOProvider seam:

THE ACCESS-API CONTRACT ALREADY EXISTS: interpreter/cobol/file_drivers.py defines FileOrganizationDriver — a runtime_checkable Protocol with a uniform, OPERATION-COMPLETE method set: open/close/read_seq/read_key/start(browse)/write/rewrite/delete. jackal-vxb's access face should ADOPT/re-export this Protocol as its contract, NOT invent a new one. The 'implicit surface' is FileOrganizationDriver (the Protocol) — NOT RealFileIOProvider (which is merely red-dragon's COBOL *adapter*: it maps VM __cobol_* calls onto a driver; it's the reference shape for jackal's own CobolIOProvider).

DECOUPLING: driver logic is clean (depends only on Path, OpenMode enum, IOResult dataclass; no VM/executor/ASG) and is already used standalone by jackal/idcams/executor.py. ONE WRINKLE: IOResult is defined in io_provider.py, which does 'from interpreter.vm.vm import Operators' — so importing a driver transitively pulls the VM. Benign for jackal (it runs the VM anyway), but the storage substrate is not truly VM-free. If a VM-independent dataset library is ever wanted, IOResult must move to a leaf module. Note for the spec, not a blocker.

COMPLETENESS: operation-complete (full CRUD + sequential + keyed + STARTBR positioning); ORG-partial. Present: PS (SequentialDriver), KSDS (IndexedDriver), RRDS (RelativeDriver — already there, so 1o2.21's RRDS half is substrate-ready; only ESDS is genuinely missing). Missing: ESDS, AIX, PDS members — these are NEW FileOrganizationDriver implementations (or member-routing for PDS) under the SAME Protocol, not a redesign.

IMPLICATION: jackal-vxb is 'consolidate + observe over a solid substrate', NOT 'build a storage engine'. Access face = pick driver by org -> add observability trace -> serve TWO client shapes (a CobolIOProvider adapter for VM-driven COBOL record I/O + status codes; direct Python calls for IDCAMS/SORT/IEBGENER). The CobolIOProvider injection seam (run(io_provider=...)) is how COBOL access plugs in -> COBOL becomes a FULLY-TRACED consumer (not binding-only), the observability-first payoff. Substrate (the 3 drivers) stays red-dragon's; jackal wraps, never reimplements.
RE-SCOPED (2026-06-25): the storage ENGINE (access + neutral outcomes) moved to a red-dragon epic (shared across the mainframe stack — see red-dragon docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-25-shared-access-method-engine-design.md). jackal-vxb is now JUST the jackal dataset CATALOG (DSN->dataset, DISP lifecycle, GDG generations, PDS members) that CONSUMES the red-dragon engine + maps neutral outcomes -> COBOL FILE STATUS. Observability/tracing deferred. This becomes actionable only after the red-dragon engine's first piece lands and is bumped in.

title: JCL parser via ANTLR grammar behind a Java bridge (proleap-bridge pattern); retire Lark
description: Foundation for thorough JCL coverage. ARCHITECTURE (decided): adopt a mature ANTLR4 JCL grammar in JAVA and call it from Python through a bridge, exactly like red-dragon's proleap-bridge does for COBOL — NOT a pure-Python ANTLR target. The bridge parses JCL (Java/ANTLR) and serializes a structured AST (JSON) back to Python; jackal deserializes into its EXISTING frozen model (Job/Step/DD/Disp). The hand-written Lark grammar (jackal/jcl/grammar.lark + Transformer) is retired. Candidate grammar: cschneid-the-elder/mapa (MIT) — bridge route means its embedded Java actions + symbolic-substitution + disposition analysis are REUSED, not stripped (the key advantage over pure-Python generation). Tasks: (1) spike — confirm mapa's JCL .g4 parses the real CardDemo jobs in Java; (2) stand up the bridge (extend proleap-bridge or a sibling jcl-bridge JAR; a JclSerializer -> JSON like StatementSerializer/AsgSerializer); (3) Python side calls the bridge via RealSubprocessRunner + bridge JAR (build product, like proleap), deserializes to the model; (4) migrate v2 features (in-stream, SYSOUT) + delete Lark; (5) re-green full suite + gated CardDemo e2e. RUNTIME: JVM per parse (already paid for COBOL). Attribution: keep upstream LICENSE/provenance.
design: Open design forks for the spec: (a) extend the EXISTING proleap-bridge JAR vs a SEPARATE jcl-bridge JAR; (b) mapa vs grossvater/jcl-parser as the grammar; (c) serialization contract (JSON shape) JCL-bridge -> Python. Must reproduce 100% of current Lark parse behavior (incl. in-stream/SYSOUT/the e2e jobs) before merge. Spike de-risks (a)/(b) before committing.
notes: SPIKE RESULT (2026-06-21): GO — grammar = cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT. JCL grammar at mapa/jcl/src/JCLParser.g4 (1002L) + JCLLexer.g4 (5096L), start rule 'startRule', tokenVocab=JCLLexer. ACTION-FREE (2 lexer-mode brace sites only) -> clean for a thin Java bridge. Coverage present: JOB/EXEC(PGM=/PROC=)/DD + per-param rules (DISP/DSN/SPACE/SYSOUT/UNIT/VOLUME/COND), in-stream (DD */DATA/DLM, grammar-native), DD concatenation, COND=, IF/ELSE/ENDIF, PROC/PEND + symbolics, GDG gen refs, referbacks (DSN=*.STEP.DD), JOBLIB/SYSCHK, OUTPUT, SET, INCLUDE, EXPORT. EVIDENCE: 38/38 CardDemo .jcl parse with ZERO errors via antlr4-parse (ANTLR 4.13.1); error detection verified on garbage. Column sensitivity (cols 73-80, // markers) handled INSIDE the lexer -> no 80-col pre-splitting needed. In-stream/SYSIN grammar-native -> no manual extraction. Separate JCLPP preprocessor grammar exists for symbolic/INCLUDE expansion — DESIGN FORK: parse raw structure (sufficient now; 38/38 was raw) vs run JCLPP first (needed for PROC/symbolics, 1o2.2). grossvater/jcl-parser REJECTED: Apache-2.0 but action-heavy, needs custom Java lexer, semantically weak (opaque FIELD_ID/params, no DISP/COND/GDG rules). Java glue needed: small — a main that runs lexer+parser and serializes the tree to JSON on stdout (proleap-bridge shape).
close_reason: Merged to main (9a7ec7d). JCL parsed via mapa ANTLR grammar behind jcl-bridge Java bridge; Lark retired; 42 tests green incl gated CardDemo e2e + parse-sweep (TRANBKP/DEFGDGB now parse). Malformed-JSON->JclParseError. Carried follow-ups (non-blocking): PROC= parsing untested (1o2.2), no Java unit test.

title: Generation Data Groups (GDG): relative + absolute generation refs
description: GDGs (DSN=A.B.C(+1), (0), (-1)) are pervasive for dated/cyclic batch datasets. Add a GDG base + generation model to the catalog: define a GDG base (IDCAMS DEFINE GDG or pre-seeded), resolve (+1)=new generation, (0)=current, (-n)=nth prior; roll generations on job completion per DISP. Without this, jobs referencing generation datasets fail to resolve DSNs.
design: Catalog gains a GDG registry mapping base -> ordered generation list; DSN resolution interprets the (gen) suffix at allocate time; (+1) allocations are cataloged on step/job success per normal disposition. Parse the (gen) suffix in the DSN grammar token, not regex.

title: Step-level conditional execution: COND= (RC-gated step bypass)
description: Steps currently always run regardless of prior return codes. Add JCL-level COND= on EXEC cards (and job-level COND=) to bypass steps based on prior step return codes: COND=(code,op[,stepname]) — bypass this step if 'code op RC' is true (operands reversed); multiple conditions COND=((c,op),(c,op)) bypass if ANY is true. CardDemo uses (0,NE) ('skip if any prior step failed') and (4,LT) pervasively. RC-only scope: no COND=EVEN/ONLY, no JCL IF/THEN/ENDIF (those are split to a sibling issue; IDCAMS-level IF/THEN already works). Runner gains per-step RC state; bypassed steps -> StepResult(ran=False).
design: Grammar: extend exec_card for COND=; add if_stmt/else/endif statements at the job level (Lark, no regex). Runner: maintain a step-RC map; evaluate conditions before dispatch; mark skipped steps in JobResult (ran=False, distinct from RC). COND= semantics are inverted ('bypass if true') — document carefully. IF/THEN is the modern, clearer form; COND= the legacy form — support both.
notes: ARCH-REVIEW CROSS-REF (2026-06-22): the whole-branch review of 1o2.9 independently flagged the same root issue this covers — cobol_step.py hardcodes StepResult return_code=0 (cobol_step.py:66), the runner never checks step RCs so a job never aborts on failure, and Disp.abnormal is modelled but dead (never consulted by catalog.dispose). All resolved by this issue's plan: wire real RETURN-CODE via read_return_code(vm), thread RC into step sequencing, and (for abnormal disp) branch dispose on step success/failure. The StepResult.ran->StepDisposition enum chosen here also addresses the review's boolean-blindness note.
close_reason: Merged to main. COND= conditional step execution: real COBOL RETURN-CODE (Part 1), Cond/CondOp model + StepDisposition, pure should_bypass (IBM reversed operands), bridge emits cond (execParmCOND/jobParmCOND), runner fold bypasses steps. 7 tasks subagent-driven, final review Ready-to-merge, full suite 71 green incl real-COBOL COND e2e. EVEN/ONLY+IF/THEN fail loud -> deferred to 1o2.8. Follow-up: jackal-449 (condFromWords silent catch).

title: Broaden jackal JCL execution coverage beyond the v2 vertical slice
description: jackal v2 proved one deep vertical slice (IDCAMS provision/load -> COBOL read, byte-faithful EBCDIC, real CardDemo ACCTFILE->READACCT). This epic broadens coverage toward 'understand/execute useful JCL'. STRATEGY CHANGE: rather than grow the hand-written Lark grammar feature-by-feature, ADOPT a mature reference ANTLR4 JCL grammar (candidate: cschneid-the-elder/mapa, MIT — already does symbolic substitution + dataset disposition) and GENERATE A PURE-PYTHON PARSER from it (ANTLR Python3 target: Java at build time, antlr4-python3-runtime at runtime; no JVM per parse). This makes thorough PARSING a one-shot foundation; the remaining gap sub-projects then become EXECUTION-semantics work layered on the parsed model. Tier model: Tier0 skeleton (DONE), Tier1 execution-shaping JCL (COND/IF, PROC/symbolics, GDG, DD concatenation, referbacks, && temp, DCB), Tier2 utility control-languages (IDCAMS partial, SORT, IEBGENER — each its own embedded language), Tier3 operational tail (mostly skip). Re-prioritized by REAL CardDemo leverage: GDG(14 jobs) > COND(5) > SORT/IEBGENER(4) > IDCAMS-depth(61 steps); PROC dropped to P3 (0 CardDemo jobs use cataloged/instream PROCs).
design: Priority order reflects what blocks running MORE real jobs: (1) step-level control flow (COND/IF) — jobs branch on RC; (2) PROC + symbolic params — most real JCL is unparseable without them; (3) SORT/IEBGENER — every batch chain sorts/copies; then GDG, DD concatenation, IDCAMS breadth, SYSOUT capture. title: COBOL: pseudo-conversational reenter flag lost — DFHCOMMAREA reference-mod group-slice MOVE shifts bytes ~12
description:
Driving real CardDemo COACTVWC turn 5 (account-id entry) revealed the reenter gate never fires: COACTVWC always takes the CDEMO-PGM-ENTER first-display branch instead of CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, so 9000-READ-ACCT (the 3 VSAM reads) never executes.

ROOT CAUSE (COBOL-FRONTEND, silent data bug, no warning): the reenter flag CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT (PIC 9(01); 88 CDEMO-PGM-REENTER; defined in copybook COCOM01Y, nested 05 CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO then 10 CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) is at rel offset 33 of the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA. On entry COACTVWC copies the inbound commarea via a reference-modified group-slice MOVE of the DFHCOMMAREA linkage group into the WS CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, then EVALUATEs the 88-levels.

OBSERVED: after turn 4 the persisted commarea has the EBCDIC '1' (0xF1) flag at byte 45 instead of byte 33 -- a consistent ~12-byte shift, with the CDEMO-GENERAL-INFO header (bytes 0-32) blank. DECISIVE: hand-building a clean inbound commarea with the flag correctly at offset 33 STILL takes first-display -- so the inbound reference-modified group-slice MOVE mis-aligns the bytes (the slice writes/reads ~12 bytes off), and/or the nested 88-level evaluation reads the wrong byte. Simple isolated SET-88 + group ref-mod cases round-trip correctly, so the trigger is the reference-modified GROUP-slice MOVE over a LINKAGE/DFHCOMMAREA region combined with a deeply-nested-copybook 88-level.

REPRO: drive tests/integration/cics/test_carddemo_signon_real.py through a 5th turn (ACCTSID entry into COACTVWC) -- COACTVWC never RECEIVEs/READs. Likely minimal repro: a program with a COCOM01Y-style nested commarea, MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:len) TO group, then test the 88-level on a field at a non-zero nested offset.

LAYER: COBOL-FRONTEND (reference-modified group-slice MOVE materialization over LINKAGE / nested-group byte addressing). NOT core VM, NOT VSAM, NOT CICS-layer. Blocks every pseudo-conversational reenter flow.
close_reason: Root cause: ProLeap bridge serialized 'LENGTH OF <group>' inside a ref-mod expression as a bogus {kind:ref,name:'LENGTHOF...'} (getText glue) -> eval_ref_mod_expr resolved it to 0 -> ref-mod start/length collapsed, shifting bytes by LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA (12). Fixed: bridge serializeBasisCtx emits {kind:length_of}; ref_mod.py RefModLengthOf variant; lower_arithmetic resolves it to byte_length. COACTVWC reenter branch now fires -> reaches 9000-READ-ACCT. Commit 442179c1; full suite 14057 green.

title: BMS loader cannot parse real BMS macro source (continuation lines); extracts 0 maps from CardDemo, masked by test stubs
description:
interpreter/cics/bms/loader.py::_parse_bms_file is a minimal regex parser that extracts ZERO maps/fields from real BMS macro source. Verified: BmsLoader(maps_dir=aws-mainframe-carddemo/app/bms) -> maps loaded: []. The CICS integration/durable tests therefore register hand-fabricated STUB maps (register_stub) with invented contiguous offsets, masking that real BMS maps don't load.

ROOT CAUSES (multiple):
1. Continuation-line format: real BMS uses col-72 '-' continuations, so a single DFHMDF's params (ATTRB/COLOR/LENGTH/POS/INITIAL) span several physical lines. The regex (\w+)\s+DFHMDF\s+.*?POS=\((\d+),(\d+)\).*?LENGTH=(\d+) matches only within one line and in a FIXED order (POS before LENGTH). Real maps often put LENGTH before POS. -> no match -> 0 fields -> map never committed (if current_map and fields).
2. Multi-map mapsets: the parser iterates ALL DFHMDI (resetting fields each time) then SEPARATELY iterates ALL DFHMDF across the WHOLE file into one dict, assigning them to the LAST map only. A mapset with multiple DFHMDI maps is broken.
3. Unlabeled fields: literal/label-only DFHMDF (e.g. 'Tran :' prompt) have a blank name field; regex (\w+) would mis-bind to the next token.
4. Offset model is WRONG for the symbolic map: offset=(row-1)*80+(col-1) computes a 3270 SCREEN position. But the COBOL symbolic map (e.g. CACTVWAO/CACTVWAI from cpy-bms/COACTVW.CPY) lays fields out as sequential L(halfword)+A(attr)+data triplets, NOT screen positions. So even if fields parsed, the offsets wouldn't match what SEND/RECEIVE MAP reads/writes in working storage.
5. It is itself regex string-surgery (.upper() whole file + finditer) of the kind the project avoids.

DESIRED: a real BMS macro parser (handle col-72 continuations, DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF with arbitrary param order, ATTRB/OCCURS/PICIN/PICOUT/GRPNAME, multi-map mapsets) that produces the SYMBOLIC-MAP layout (offsets/lengths matching the generated COBOL copybook field structure), so SEND/RECEIVE MAP exercise REAL maps loaded from app/bms instead of stubs. Likely should align with / derive from the symbolic copybook (cpy-bms/*.CPY) which our COBOL layout engine already parses, rather than re-deriving from the BMS macro. Cross-check the two.

IMPACT: blocks faithful end-to-end CICS emulation (real screens). Currently every CICS test uses stub maps. Surfaced while extending the durable real-CardDemo test to COACTVWC turn 4 (map CACTVWA). Related: red-dragon-pz9g.5 (BMS Screen Engine), red-dragon-pz9g.10 (symbolic maps).
notes:
SPEC-vs-CODE DIVERGENCE (root of this gap): plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-06-cics-E-bms.md Task E1 specified bms-tools (a PROPER BMS grammar/library) vendored as a git submodule at vendor/bms-tools/ (url https://github.com/MikeB-ACS/bms-tools). The plan included a fallback: 'If bms-tools is not available as a public submodule, use a minimal stub.' The shipped implementation took the FALLBACK — no vendor/, no submodule (.gitmodules has only proleap), just the inline regex _parse_bms_file in interpreter/cics/bms/loader.py. The specified repo MikeB-ACS/bms-tools no longer resolves (deleted/renamed/private) and is not on PyPI; web search finds no maintained 'bms-tools' parser (only mainframed/ANSi2BMS, a generator). So the proper-grammar path was never realized and the fallback stub can't parse real BMS.

CANDIDATE FIX DIRECTIONS (decide):
(A) Write our own proper BMS grammar (Lark) in-repo: DFHMSD/DFHMDI/DFHMDF, col-72 continuations, arbitrary param order, multi-map mapsets, ATTRB/OCCURS/PICIN/PICOUT. Produces map field layout. We own it; consistent with the CICS command Lark grammar.
(B) Derive the map layout from the SYMBOLIC COPYBOOK (cpy-bms/*.CPY, e.g. COACTVW.CPY defining CACTVWAI/CACTVWAO) which our ProLeap COBOL layout engine ALREADY parses — single source of truth, no new parser. SEND/RECEIVE MAP read <base>O/<base>I from that group, so the symbolic-map offsets/lengths are exactly what's needed; screen POS/ATTRB (only in the .bms macro) are not needed for value-level field extraction. Eliminates the regex parser entirely.
(C) Locate/vendor a maintained third-party BMS parser — uncertain availability.

Note: (B) likely the best engineering fit (reuses existing COBOL copybook layout; the symbolic copybook is the actual contract SEND/RECEIVE MAP operate on). (A) needed only if real 3270 screen geometry/attributes are later required.
close_reason: Replaced the regex _parse_bms_file stub with the full bms-tools pipeline. BmsLoader/BmsMap/BmsField deleted; stage-0 generate_symbolic_copybooks (hlasm_export | bms-copybook-gen, gated on BMS_TOOLS_HOME) emits symbolic copybooks into a dir wired into copybook_dirs; SEND/RECEIVE MAP read/write the symbolic group's fields from data_layout (field names resolved at lowering from the static FROM/INTO group via MaterialisedSectionedLayout.group_leaf_names). Durable + synthetic CICS tests migrated off stubs. Full suite 14054 green; 0 BmsLoader refs. NOTE: end-to-end run of the durable test requires the locally-built C++ hlasm_export binary (test skips until BMS_TOOLS_HOME points at a built ~/code/bms-tools); wiring verified, e2e gated.

title: CICS SEND/RECEIVE MAP: MAP()/MAPSET() data-name operands lowered as literal Const, not resolved to runtime value
description:
SEND MAP / RECEIVE MAP lowering in interpreter/cics/strategy.py (~445-450 for SEND, ~RECEIVE path) emits the MAP and MAPSET operands as hardcoded literal Const(value=opts.get('MAP',...)). When the operand is a quoted literal (MAP('COSGN0A')) this happens to work, but when it is a DATA-NAME (MAP(CCARD-NEXT-MAP) / MAP(LIT-THISMAP)) the literal STRING 'CCARD-NEXT-MAP' is passed to the BMS loader instead of the field's runtime value ('CACTVWA'), so loader.get() misses, the screen builtin takes the unknown-map branch, and no symbolic <base>O fields are emitted (empty screen fields).

This is the standard CardDemo screen idiom (MOVE LIT-THISMAP TO CCARD-NEXT-MAP; SEND MAP(CCARD-NEXT-MAP)), so it blocks every CardDemo screen program beyond the two sign-on/menu programs that use literal map names. Surfaced driving real COACTVWC turn 4 (COACTVWC.cbl:583 SEND, :611 RECEIVE).

FIX: replace the two Const emits with emit_operand_value(ctx, opts.get('MAP'/'MAPSET'), materialised) (strategy.py:93) which already strips quotes for literals AND resolves data-names via ctx.resolve_field_ref + emit_decode_field -- exactly as XCTL PROGRAM (strategy.py:400) and READ FILE (508,563) do. Apply to BOTH SEND MAP and RECEIVE MAP (MAP + MAPSET operands). CICS-layer only; do NOT touch core (vm/ir/run/executor).

TDD: unit test that SEND/RECEIVE MAP with a data-name operand resolves to its runtime value (mirror tests/unit/cics/test_operand_value.py style); integration test: COBOL program MOVEs a map name into WS then SEND MAP(WS-VAR) and assert the screen carries the resolved map name + a field. After fix, the real COACTVWC turn 4 renders CACTVWA.
close_reason: Stale — already fixed. cics/strategy.py:699 resolves MAP()/MAPSET() operands via emit_operand_value (present since the interpreter/cics/ -> cics/ migration, commit 2a5922f, which postdates this issue). Verified live: tests/integration/cics/test_region_e2e.py::test_send_map_data_name_resolves_runtime_value (docstring cites g5gx) passes; full 66-test tests/integration/cics/ suite passes under JDK 17.

title: CICS: subscripted option operand resolves to element 1 (emit_operand_value drops the subscript offset)
description:
XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) (and any subscripted CICS option operand) resolves to the FIRST table element, not the indexed one. The CICS parser captures the subscripted text (pz9g.18) and the COBOL frontend's uniform resolver already handles it: emit_operand_value -> ctx.resolve_field_ref -> parse_subscript_notation splits NAME(SUB), resolves the base, and computes the element offset into ref.offset_reg. But emit_operand_value (interpreter/cics/strategy.py) calls ctx.emit_decode_field(region_reg, ref.fl) WITHOUT ref.offset_reg, so emit_decode_field falls back to the base field offset (element 1) and the subscript is ignored.

Fix: pass ref.offset_reg -> ctx.emit_decode_field(region_reg, ref.fl, ref.offset_reg). One line; routes the operand straight from parser through the uniform COBOL field resolver (no CICS-layer subscript special-casing). Affects all operands resolved via emit_operand_value (RETURN TRANSID, XCTL PROGRAM, VSAM FILE/DATASET) uniformly. Bare (non-subscripted) operands are unaffected (their offset_reg is the base offset). Surfaced extending the real CardDemo flow to a menu option selection (COMEN01C XCTLs PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION))).
acceptance_criteria: XCTL PROGRAM(TBL(IDX)) resolves to the value of element IDX (e.g. element 2 = 'COADM01C'); RETURN TRANSID and VSAM FILE/DATASET subscripted operands likewise; bare operands still work.
close_reason: emit_operand_value now passes ref.offset_reg to emit_decode_field, so subscripted CICS operands (XCTL PROGRAM(WS-PGM(WS-IDX)) etc.) resolve the indexed element via the COBOL frontend's uniform resolve_field_ref. One-line fix, no CICS-layer subscript logic. JAR-gated test asserts element 2 resolves; full suite green.

title: CICS parser: subscripted option value PROGRAM(X(idx)) + NOHANDLE flag not parsed
description:
The Lark CICS command parser (interpreter/cics/cics_parser.py) fails on an option value that is a SUBSCRIPTED data-name with nested parentheses, e.g.:
    EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE
ValueError: Cannot parse EXEC CICS text: 'INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE'. The grammar treats '(' .. ')' as the option-value delimiter, so the inner ')' of the subscript closes the option early and the rest ('(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE') is unparseable. Also NOHANDLE is a bare flag keyword that must be accepted.

Surfaced extending the real CardDemo flow to the menu: COMEN01C (transid CM00) uses option-table lookups  and won't even COMPILE today.

Fix: extend the CICS command grammar so an option value may contain balanced nested parentheses (a subscripted reference), and accept NOHANDLE (and likely other bare flags) as a flag option. Scope: cics_parser.py grammar + tests; CICS layer only. NOTE: a subscripted option operand also needs downstream resolution at lowering (XCTL/INQUIRE PROGRAM(table(idx))) — resolve the subscripted data-name to its runtime value, like the OF-qualified/leaf-name work; may be a follow-up once parsing works.
acceptance_criteria: EXEC CICS INQUIRE PROGRAM(CDEMO-MENU-OPT-PGMNAME(WS-OPTION)) NOHANDLE parses (verb INQUIRE, option PROGRAM with the subscripted operand text, NOHANDLE flag); COMEN01C compiles. Simple option values still parse.
close_reason: CICS grammar now parses subscripted option values via a recursive value/value_part rule (balanced nested parens, no regex balancing); NOHANDLE flag parses. 16 parser tests, full CICS suite green. Pure-Python (no JAR). NOTE: downstream resolution of a subscripted option operand (e.g. INQUIRE/XCTL PROGRAM(table(idx))) to its runtime value may be a follow-up.

title: COBOL: intrinsic FUNCTION argument that is an OF-qualified data-name is getText-concatenated, not resolved
description:
FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) operates on the mangled field-name text instead of the field's value. Diagnostic (real COSGN00C sign-on): the READ RIDFLD key came out as EBCDIC 'USERIDIO' = getText('USERIDI OF COSGN0AI') = 'USERIDIOFCOSGN0AI' truncated to the 8-char key field, instead of the value 'USER0001'. So UPPER-CASE upper-cased the concatenated qualified-name text, not the operand.

Root cause: the 8eiq bridge function-argument serialization (StatementSerializer.java serializeFunctionArg / serializeFunctionNode*, added in red-dragon-8eiq) does NOT structurally resolve a qualified (OF/IN) data-name argument to its leaf field reference — it falls back to a getText()-style concatenation. A simple-field arg (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(WS-X)) works; an OF-qualified arg does not.

Fix: serialize each function argument as a structured operand using the same data-reference extraction the rest of the serializer uses (leaf name 'USERIDI', dropping the 'OF COSGN0AI' qualification — red-dragon resolves by leaf name), i.e. emit {kind:ref,name:USERIDI} (or the proper operand node) rather than concatenated text. Then the frontend's existing arg lowering decodes USERIDI to its value and UPPER-CASE works. Scope: bridge (COBOL serializer) + tests; stays in the COBOL layer, no core engine changes. This is the last known blocker before the real CardDemo sign-on READ finds the user and XCTLs to COMEN01C.
acceptance_criteria: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) yields the uppercased VALUE of USERIDI (e.g. 'USER0001'); the real sign-on READ key matches the seeded record. Simple-field function args still work. No core-engine edits.
close_reason: OF-qualified data-name in function/expr args now resolves to the leaf field via leafDataName() (first dataName of qualifiedDataNameFormat1) instead of getText() flattening. FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI OF COSGN0AI) -> USERIDI value. Bridge-only, no core. VERIFIED: real CardDemo sign-on (COSGN00C) now reaches XCTL to COMEN01C end-to-end.

title: CICS: READ/STARTBR DATASET(...) keyword + data-name file operand not resolved (returns RESP_DISABLED)
description:
EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-USRSEC-FILE) ... never resolves the dataset -> engine returns RESP_DISABLED (84), so the READ never consults the key and the program's EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD hits WHEN OTHER. Two defects in the VSAM lowering (interpreter/cics/strategy.py, the _VSAM_POINT_VERBS branch ~line 505 and the browse branch ~line 559):
1. KEYWORD: it reads only opts.get('FILE'). CICS allows DATASET(...) as a synonym for FILE(...). CardDemo uses DATASET. So opts.get('FILE') is None -> file_name lowered as empty/None.
2. DATA-NAME OPERAND: even with the DATASET alias, the operand WS-USRSEC-FILE is a DATA-NAME (PIC X(8) VALUE 'USRSEC  '), not a literal. The lowering currently emits Const(opts.get('FILE')) — the field NAME — instead of resolving the field's runtime VALUE. Must resolve it like RETURN TRANSID/XCTL PROGRAM did (red-dragon-pz9g.13, emit_operand_value): if the operand names a field, decode it to its runtime value; else literal. The VsamEngine already strips spaces/quotes and upper-cases, so a resolved 'USRSEC  ' matches a dataset registered as USRSEC.

Apply to READ/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE (FILE/DATASET) and STARTBR (FILE/DATASET). Surfaced re-spiking the real sign-on (COSGN00C reads USRSEC via DATASET(WS-USRSEC-FILE)). Confirmed: engine.read got file_name='None', keylen=8 (LENGTH OF works), RESP=84.
acceptance_criteria: READ/STARTBR/WRITE/REWRITE/DELETE accept DATASET(...) as a synonym for FILE(...); a data-name file operand resolves to its runtime value (WS-USRSEC-FILE -> 'USRSEC') so the engine finds the dataset; literal file names still work.
close_reason: VSAM lowering accepts DATASET(...) as synonym for FILE(...) and resolves a data-name file operand to its runtime value via emit_operand_value. JAR-gated round-trip test with DATASET(WS-DSN). CICS-layer only, no core touch. Full suite green.

title: CICS: RETURN TRANSID / XCTL PROGRAM with a data-name operand lowers the name as a literal
description: EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) yields DispatchResult(transid='WS-TRANID') -- the field NAME -- instead of the field's VALUE ('CC00'), so the dispatcher cannot route and ABENDs TRNI. CicsLoweringStrategy.lower emits Const(value=opts.get('TRANSID')) for the RETURN/XCTL operands, always treating them as literals and never resolving a data-name to its runtime value. Same literal-only treatment applies to XCTL PROGRAM(data-name) (works only when a literal program name is used). Fix: when the TRANSID/PROGRAM operand names a data item, resolve+decode it (the F-machinery emit_copy_in / field decode) and pass the runtime value; keep the literal fast-path. strategy.py ~line 354.
acceptance_criteria: RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) routes by the field's value; XCTL PROGRAM(WS-PGM) resolves the runtime program name; literal forms still work.
close_reason: Fixed with TDD (emit_operand_value resolves data-name operands); full suite green.

title: CICS: HANDLE CONDITION/AID runtime-dispatch machinery (deferred)
description: Exact emulation of HANDLE CONDITION/AID the way production CICS does it: a per-execution runtime handler table (condition/AID -> label) plus a computed branch after each fallible command (mirrors the IBM translator's GO TO ... DEPENDING ON). NOT static path analysis — handler activation is a runtime property. The VM already has the computed-branch primitive (BranchIf with a cond_reg + branch_targets tuple). DEFERRED: the target online tier uses HANDLE AID 0x and HANDLE CONDITION 1x (an off-happy-path PGMIDERR guard, currently a safe no-op), so this is not needed today. Build when a program relies on condition/AID handlers that affect the happy path.
design: Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-07-cics-handle-condition-machinery.md. Three parts: (1) runtime HandlerTable holder reset at program entry; (2) HANDLE* lowers to runtime table writes (order/override/loops honored naturally); (3) after each fallible command emit BranchIf(cond_reg, branch_targets=(handler labels)) keyed on EIBRESP/condition, and after RECEIVE MAP keyed on EIBAID. Scope per CICS: effective to end of program, overridable, not propagated to sub-programs.
notes:
Re-measured 2026-09-02 on the full production online corpus (2,137 programs), two orders of magnitude larger than the 9-file sample that promoted this to P1: 2,679 HANDLE CONDITION occurrences across 1,599 of 2,137 programs — 75%. Plus IGNORE CONDITION at 820 (in scope here, per the note above) and HANDLE AID at 10. This is the largest-radius defect in docs/analysis/2026-09-01-index-items-search-and-cics-verb-gaps.md.

Scope split made explicit: this bead is the HANDLER TABLE AND DISPATCH half. The other half — that nothing ever RAISES a condition in the first place, because emit_resp_writeback only writes EIBRESP and returns — is forge-5by. Per the analysis's sequencing note the two should land TOGETHER: raising without dispatch converts a large number of silent wrong answers into abends, which is more truthful but reads as a regression in any pass/fail count.

The plan named in the DESIGN field (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-07-cics-handle-condition-machinery.md) DOES NOT EXIST in this repository — 'find . -name "*handle-condition*"' returns nothing. It never survived the monorepo migration and must be rewritten from scratch; do not go looking for it.
close_reason:
Half done, and the remaining half is tracked separately, so closing this rather than leaving it to describe work that no longer matches the code.

HANDLE CONDITION is implemented (1917ed0c..97ea2c61, see forge-5by): a runtime handler table numbered per program, a raise tail after each fallible command, and a per-program dispatcher. This bead's prediction held — the machinery is runtime, not static analysis, and BranchIf was the primitive. One correction to its wording: BranchIf is strictly TWO-way, so the computed branch is a comparison cascade following _lower_computed_goto, not a single n-way instruction.

HANDLE AID is still a registered no-op and is carried forward as forge-xcs.

Also obsolete in the deferral rationale: the guard it calls 'a safe no-op' is no longer safe now that conditions raise — an unhandled condition abends AEIZ rather than falling through.

title: CICS: HANDLE CONDITION/AID real semantics + EIBAID write-back
description: HANDLE CONDITION, HANDLE AID and HANDLE ABEND are all currently aliased to a single no-op builtin (__cics_handle_abend). Two real semantics are missing: (1) HANDLE CONDITION/AID must register a label and cause a branch to it after subsequent commands when the condition/AID fires; (2) EIBAID is never written into the EIB between turns — the RECEIVE MAP / dispatcher path drops the attention key. CardDemo menu navigation and program exit branch on EIBAID (e.g. IF EIBAID = DFHPF3) and on HANDLE AID, so without these, PF-key navigation does not work.
design: EIBAID: when an input event arrives (RECEIVE MAP or between pseudo-conversational turns), write its attention id into the EIB region (same mechanism as init_eib's EIBAID write). Depends on field-ref/EIB write path from pz9g.7. HANDLE: epic DESIGN prescribes 'CALL __cics_handle(...) + injected BRANCH_IF after subsequent commands; prefer normalizing to RESP-check form where CardDemo allows.' Translator records the handler label and emits conditional branches; start with the RESP-check normalization where possible, fall back to label-branch injection.
acceptance_criteria: EIBAID reflects the terminal attention key inside the program; HANDLE AID branches to the registered label on the matching key; covered by unit + integration tests.
notes:
Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-handle-eibaid-design.md
AUDIT (18 online programs): HANDLE AID used 0x; HANDLE CONDITION used 1x (off happy path, now explicit no-op). So this story reduces to EIBAID write-back only (navigation uses IF EIBAID = DFHPFnn directly). Faithful HANDLE machinery split out as a separate deferred story; see plan 2026-06-07-cics-handle-condition-machinery.md.

title: CICS Sub-project F: EXEC CICS field-ref wiring + BY-REFERENCE copy-back
description: ROOT GAP. Implementation of sub-projects A-E lowers EXEC CICS verbs to CallFunction with Const placeholder args (empty bytes / literals). No option data-name is resolved to its field, and no output flows back. The CICS layer can route control flow (RETURN/XCTL/dispatch) but CANNOT MOVE APPLICATION DATA. This contradicts the epic's own architecture, which specifies: parse the command, resolve option data-names NAME-BASED at lowering time (resolve_field_ref against MaterialisedSectionedLayout), pass them BY REFERENCE, and let the existing CALL USING copy-back mechanism move outputs back. That copy-back machinery already shipped; the CICS lowering simply never used it.
design:
For each EXEC CICS option that names a COBOL data item (FROM, INTO, RIDFLD, COMMAREA, APPLID, SYSID, YYYYMMDD, TIME, RESP, LENGTH-as-ref, etc.): at lowering time in CicsLoweringStrategy.lower(), resolve the name against the MaterialisedSectionedLayout and emit a reference arg (address/region) instead of Const(b''). Literals stay literal. The builtin then reads inputs from the referenced region and writes outputs back into the caller's region via BY-REFERENCE copy-back (same path CALL USING uses).

Cascade fixed by this story:
- COMMAREA on RETURN TRANSID / XCTL actually carries state between turns (currently always empty).
- RESP(r) and EIBRESP written back after each call -> 'IF EIBRESP = DFHRESP(NORMAL)' checks work.
- ASSIGN APPLID/SYSID write the target field (builtin is currently a no-op).
- FORMATTIME YYYYMMDD/TIME output fields written.
- VSAM READ/WRITE INTO/FROM move record bytes; RIDFLD passes the key.
- SEND MAP loads the FROM area; RECEIVE MAP writes the INTO area.

Acceptance: a builtin receiving a referenced field can read its current bytes and a write is observable in VM memory after the call returns. Add unit tests per verb option and an integration test asserting COMMAREA round-trips across two turns.
acceptance_criteria: Field-named EXEC CICS options resolve to real field references (not Const placeholders); builtin reads/writes observable in VM memory; COMMAREA round-trips across a RETURN TRANSID turn; EIBRESP/RESP reflect the call outcome.
notes:
Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-cics-F-field-ref-wiring-design.md
Implementation plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-07-cics-F-field-ref-wiring.md. Decision locked: EIBRESP written lowering-side.

title: CICS milestone: sign-on -> menu flow end-to-end (screens/files stubbed)
description:
First proof-of-architecture milestone. With EIB fields, DFHAID/DFHBMSCA constants, and a dispatch trampoline that round-trips the COMMAREA, the COSGN00C (sign-on) -> COMEN01C/COADM01C (menu) navigation should FLOW even with screens and files stubbed.

Demonstrates the full pseudo-conversational loop without requiring full BMS or VSAM fidelity:
- First entry (EIBCALEN=0): program sends sign-on screen, RETURNs with TRANSID+COMMAREA.
- Re-entry on Enter (DFHENTER via EIBAID): PROCESS-ENTER-KEY runs; a stubbed user READ returns NORMAL; XCTL to the menu program carrying the COMMAREA.
- Menu program re-enters with the COMMAREA populated (from-program, user-id, user-type).

File READ (USRSEC) and SEND/RECEIVE MAP may be stubbed (canned record, no real screen) — the point is to prove EIB + dispatch + EXEC CICS control flow work together end-to-end. Full file/screen fidelity comes via the VSAM and BMS children.
acceptance_criteria: 1. COSGN00C first-entry path runs: builds sign-on screen, RETURNs with TRANSID + COMMAREA. 2. Re-entry with DFHENTER drives PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. 3. Stubbed user READ returns NORMAL and the program XCTLs to the menu program. 4. The menu program re-enters with the COMMAREA carrying user-id/user-type set by sign-on. 5. Integration test exercises the two-transaction flow via the dispatch driver.
